meta.description: A flight itinerary to support your UK visitor visa plan, with booking reference and PDF delivery. Learn what UK applicants should and should not do.

h1: Flight reservation for a UK visa
lead: Support your UK visitor visa plan with a clear itinerary, without paying for a ticket before a decision.
body: ## Do UK applications need flights?

UK visitor visa guidance generally focuses on your purpose, funds, accommodation and reasons to return home. Official advice commonly tells applicants not to buy non-refundable travel until a decision is made. An itinerary can support your plan, but it is not normally the document that decides a case. Our [UK visa flight booking guide](/blog/uk-visa-flight-booking-requirements) covers the detail.
## What you receive

- A flight reservation with a booking reference (PNR)
- Your name as it appears on the passport
- Route, dates and flight numbers
- A PDF itinerary by email
The [sample ticket](/sample-ticket) shows the layout.
## Where an itinerary helps

- It gives a clear arrival and departure date to match your form.
- It supports an invitation letter from a host.
- It helps you plan consistent dates for accommodation and leave from work.
## Where it does not

It does not prove that you can afford the trip, and it does not explain why you will return home. Bank statements, employment letters and other documents do that. If you were refused before, an itinerary will not resolve the reason.
> A reservation is not a ticket and does not guarantee a visa. We cannot promise that any decision-maker will accept it.
## Keep dates consistent
A strong UK file shows the same dates everywhere: form, itinerary, accommodation, leave letter and invitation. If a date changes, change the plan and order a fresh itinerary. Never edit the PDF.
## Related options
Applying to more than one destination? See the [US visa page](/dummy-ticket-for-us-visa) and [Schengen visa page](/dummy-ticket-for-schengen-visa). For pricing, see [pricing](/pricing).
## Using it honestly

Describe a reservation as a reservation. If you are asked for a paid ticket, a refundable fare is the right answer. See [dummy ticket vs real flight booking](/blog/dummy-ticket-vs-real-flight-booking).
## What a strong UK file looks like

A consistent file reads the same everywhere. The form lists an arrival and departure date, the itinerary matches them, the accommodation covers the nights in between, and any host's invitation names the same period. Funds are shown with recent statements, and reasons to return home are shown with employment, study or family documents. Nothing in the file has to be dramatic; it simply has to agree with itself.
## If you are asked for more

Sometimes a caseworker asks for additional documents. Reply by the deadline, send exactly what was asked and keep your explanation short and factual. If you are asked for a paid ticket specifically, treat that as a direct instruction and follow it with a refundable fare if you can.
## Families and groups

When several people apply together, each person needs their own itinerary entry with the correct passport name. For children travelling with only one parent or another adult, check the current guidance on consent letters. Our [visa application checklist](/blog/visa-application-checklist) covers the other documents to prepare.

Q: Do I need to book a flight for a UK visitor visa?
A: Guidance generally does not require a purchased ticket and advises against non-refundable fares before a decision. Check the current official guidance for your application.

Q: Can a reservation replace a paid ticket?
A: Only if the authority accepts it. We cannot promise acceptance.
